extraction.name: Science Question Answering (SCIENCEQA)
extraction.description: A benchmark containing 21,208 multimodal multiple-choice questions from elementary and high school curricula, spanning natural science, social science, and language science across grades 1–12. Questions cover 26 topics, 127 categories, and 379 skills. Examples include answer options, a correct answer, optional textual and image contexts, and, for most questions, grounded lectures and explanations.
extraction.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; available for non-commercial research purposes only. Copyright belongs to the original authors, identified in the checklist as IXL.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, and Ashwin Kalyan. Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022). arXiv:2209.09513v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Original science problems were downloaded from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by K–12 education experts. Individual components, including questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions, were extracted using heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed, lectures and solutions were reformatted with semi-automated scripts, and experts reviewed examples and manually revised incorrect annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Not all questions contain contexts, lectures, or explanations. Of 21,208 questions, 10,220 have text context, 10,332 have image context, 6,532 have both, and 7,188 have neither. Table 1 reports 17,798 questions with lectures (83.9%) and 19,202 with explanations (90.5%). Section 3.1 instead reports that 91.3% feature an explanation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science problems from open resources managed by IXL Learning at https://www.ixl.com/, curated by experts in K–12 education and aligned with California Common Core Content Standards. Downloaded problems supplied questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: When multiple correct answers applied, only one correct answer was retained. Answer options were shuffled to avoid a specific choice pattern. Semi-automated scripts reformatted lectures and solutions so that tables and lists were distinguishable from ordinary text. The dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and test sets in a 60:20:20 ratio, containing 12,726, 4,241, and 4,241 examples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules extracted individual components from downloaded problems. Questions with only one choice, faulty data, or duplication were manually removed. Lectures and solutions were reformatted using semi-automated scripts. For language-model experiments, images were converted to captions using a ViT–GPT-2 captioning model, newline separators were escaped, and questions without context used an empty context string.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Correct answers, lectures, and solutions were extracted from the original IXL problems. Lectures provide general background knowledge, while explanations provide specific reasons for the correct answer. Experts used a data exploration tool to review collected examples and manually revise incorrect annotations. Separately, Amazon Mechanical Turk workers answered test questions for a human-performance baseline and assessed generated explanations for relevance, correctness, and completeness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Dataset exploration and review tool: https://scienceqa.github.io/explore.html. Amazon Mechanical Turk was used for the human-performance study and evaluation of model-generated explanations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Incorrect dataset annotations were manually revised by experts after review. In the human-performance study, workers who answered fewer than four of five qualification questions correctly were excluded from analysis. For evaluation of generated explanations, final human scores were determined by majority vote among three workers. A gold explanation was defined as relevant, correct, and complete.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three workers per test question in the human-performance study and three workers per generated explanation in the explanation-evaluation study. The number of human annotators per original dataset item is not stated.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human-performance study workers were required to have a high school degree or higher. The source platform was curated by experts in K–12 education, and collected annotations were reviewed and revised by experts. Further demographic specifications are not stated.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic extraction rules and semi-automated scripts were used to extract and reformat source annotations. For experimental visual-context captions, the authors used https://huggingface.co/nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning, based on ViT and GPT-2.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that antisocial data points will be removed from the dataset based on feedback. An updating timeframe, named maintainers, versioning policy, and deprecation policy are not stated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The authors explicitly state that the dataset contains no user usage data, personally identifiable information, or personally sensitive information such as gender and race.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to diagnose multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems and support research on reliable, interpretable reasoning. Potential applications include K–12 tutoring systems. The authors state that careful examination found no improper content, including pornographic information, racial remarks, or harmful social bias, to their best knowledge, and commit to removing antisocial data points based on feedback.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The majority of questions come from grades 3–8, while approximately 10% come from grades 9–12. The authors report finding no harmful social bias after careful examination, to their best knowledge. Blind studies using only questions or only image contexts produced results close to random chance, which the authors interpret as evidence of a robust and reliable distribution.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset covers grades 1–12 and problems aligned with California Common Core Content Standards. Its grade distribution is concentrated in grades 3–8, with approximately 10% of questions from high school. Lectures and explanations are not available for every question. Questions with multiple applicable correct answers were reduced to a single retained correct answer. Use is restricted to non-commercial research purposes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, testing, and fine-tuning of multimodal question-answering models; zero-shot and few-shot evaluation; benchmarking multimodal understanding, multi-hop reasoning, and generation of lectures and explanations as chains of thought. The paper also identifies potential contributions to K–12 tutoring systems. The prescribed task is to select the correct answer from multiple options given a question and available multimodal contexts, optionally generating supporting lectures and explanations. The dataset is available for non-commercial research purposes only.
